what: Server-side record of the iPhone's cloud voice for one assignment change, read after the fact: the AI Logic speech call through the pls-voice-v1 template during the build 11 iPhone session on drill-kennesaw-1. It shows that a speech call from the iOS app reached the model and succeeded; it does not show that the phone played the audio.
readBy: Read-only queries with project credentials; nothing was written
context: Reported by the iPhone session, not checked by these reads: command approved plan v2 in drill-kennesaw-1 (team T1, segment HE to GS), and the phone (Ad Hoc build 11, 1.0.0 (11), App Attest production, iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 27.2.1) showed GS within seconds. The audio recording of that moment failed.

plan.source: Firestore, incidents/drill-kennesaw-1/plans/0002, field approvedAt (server timestamp), read 2026-11-25T17:58Z

trigger.source: Cloud Logging, Cloud Run service cloudguard (the before-generate trigger)
trigger.coldStart: A new instance started for this request (autoscaling)
trigger.note: Every template call logs path direct and template null, because AI Logic expands a template before the trigger sees it (docs/SECURITY.md row 12). The rewrite added the speech model's 4,096-token output cap.

otherCalls: None: this is the only speech call in 05:26 to 05:32Z (trigger log) and the only AI Logic call in the window (metrics)

remoteConfig.source: Remote Config REST template, read at readAt

caveats: The metrics name the platform and the app version (1.0.0), not the build number or the device, so they cannot by themselves say which iPhone made the call.

The Firebase Performance trace assignment_speech (path, outcome, start_ms) was not readable here: the project has no BigQuery export and the trace is in the console only. Whether the phone played the audio is unproven.
corrections: 2026-11-25T17:58Z: templateRender.template said the metric carries no template label. It does: template_id is pls-voice-v1. The first read's label filter dropped every key containing "id". Re-read with raw labels.
2026-11-25T17:58Z: context gave the plan's approval as about 05:27:50Z, as reported. Firestore's approvedAt is 05:27:46.197Z (plan), 1.3 s before the trigger request.
